newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to extend 22 bln yen in loans to Romania - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to extend 22 bln yen in loans to Romania - MOF.

text.p: Japan plans to extend loans worth about 22 billion yen to Romania to fund infrastructure projects, a Japanese Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Monday.
It will be the first time Japan has granted yen loans to Romania or any of the former Communist nations of eastern Europe, he added.

Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told his visiting Romanian counterpart Mircea Ciumara of the decision in a meeting on Monday. Ciumara is accompanying President Emil Constantinescu on a visit to Tokyo.
Of the 22 billion yen, 12.8 billion yen will be used to develop port facilities, while the remaining 9.19 billion is to be used for road construction, the official said.
In addition, the Export-Import Bank of Japan will lend Romania $50 million as part of a co-financing project with the World Bank. The World Bank will make loans worth $280 million.
The official signing of the loans by both the Japanese government and the Export-Import Bank was scheduled to take place later on Monday, the MOF official said.
